claims: Artemis II successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
As of April 2, 2026, the Artemis II rocket and Orion spacecraft successfully lifted off.
As of April 2, 2026, the Artemis II core stage separated, placing the crew in orbit.
The Artemis II crew includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch.
The Artemis II crew includes CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II is a 10-day test flight to take the four astronauts around the Moon and back.
Artemis II marks the first crewed lunar mission since 1972.
As of April 2, 2026, the Artemis II crew is currently in the early stages of their journey.
The Artemis II crew will perform a translunar injection burn to head towards the Moon on Day 2.
The Artemis II launch marks returning humans to deep space for the first time in over 50 years.
